Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: CS transition: model spectrum, context budget and token runway

Hi Elliot / Asha —

Thanks again for the pilot sign-off. Next step from our side is the CS -> Implementation transition where we lock the model candidate list, the context length budget, and the token runway assumptions so engineering can size Dedicated capacity correctly. 

To keep the kickoff tight, can you confirm the following by EOD Friday? If easier, Asha feel free to drop the answers in Slack or reply inline.

1) Typical user prompt length (tokens) and the 90th percentile prompt length.
2) Average generative response length and 95th percentile.
3) Estimated peak concurrent sessions during product launch (QPS or users/min).
4) Which endpoints will be used: chat (multi-turn), one-shot generation, or embeddings?
5) Any PII / retention requirements (how long you need logs/inputs stored).

We attach our suggested model spectrum (small -> medium -> large with quantization profiles) and a token_profile template you can use to populate. From our side, Monica will run a quick sizing exercise and Vivek will validate kernel/quantization fit once we have the token distributions. Ben / Jordan from Sales are cc'd to align on committed capacity and billing cadence.

Next meeting suggestion: Fri 20 Apr, 11:00am PT — 30 minutes to review answers and agree on model lanes. Let me know if that slot works.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Fwd: CS transition: model spectrum, context budget and token runway

Folks — forwarding LatticeAI kickoff. Key asks are token length distributions, intended endpoints (chat vs one-shot vs embeddings), peak concurrency, and retention.

Initial thoughts from CS: target production rollout will need two model lanes (latency-sensitive small model + fallback large model for high-quality responses). If Lattice's 95th percentile prompt+response length is >4k tokens we should plan for either longer-context variants or a context-trimming approach; Vivek, can you check kernel support for 4k+ sequences on our quantized medium profile?

Monica, can you prepare a simple cost delta (per 10k tokens) for small vs medium vs large lanes so Sales can position commit options? Ben/Jordan — if Lattice commits to a 6-month reserved lane for the medium model, what discount band should we propose?

I'll take point on the Friday meeting coordination.

—Grace

Subject: Re: CS transition: model spectrum, context budget and token runway

Hi Grace / team — thanks for the clear checklist. Answers below and attached a small sample export from our staging logs (token counts by session).

1) Typical prompt length: 36 tokens; 90th percentile prompt length: 420 tokens.
2) Average generative response: 120 tokens; 95th percentile: 1,800 tokens (long explanations and code blocks).
3) Peak concurrent sessions: we expect ~85 concurrent during launch windows, roughly 2.5 QPS sustained, bursts up to 12 QPS for short periods.
4) Endpoints: primarily chat (multi-turn with 5–7 turns typical), occasional one-shot generation for summaries, and embeddings for semantic search on ~10% of calls.
5) Retention: we need request/response logs stored for 90 days for analytics; PII is scrubbed upstream but we will need access to redacted traces for debugging.

We can do the Friday 11:00am PT slot — Asha will join with product to walk through sample conversations.

Attaching: lattice_token_profile.xlsx (sample export), sample_sessions.json (redacted)

Thanks,
